playbooks.title: Claiming Unclaimed Dividends and Shares Transferred to IEPF
playbooks.legal_basis: Section 125(3) of Companies Act 2013 read with IEPF Authority (Accounting, Audit, Transfer and Refund) Rules 2016
playbooks.trigger_condition: Dividends or shares unclaimed for 7 consecutive years transferred by company to Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF)

step_by_step_process.action: Submit online e-Form IEPF-5 on the MCA portal (mca.gov.in). Fill details of claimant, company CIN, folio number/DP-Client ID, unclaimed dividend amount, and share quantity.
System generates an SRN (Service Request Number) and printable IEPF-5 acknowledgement slip.

Submit physical claim dossier to Company Nodal Officer / RTA within 15 days. Dossier must contain: Printed signed IEPF-5 form, SRN slip, Original share certificates (if physical), Cancelled cheque leaf, Advance Stamp Receipt signed with Rs 1 revenue stamp, CML of Demat Account, Aadhaar and PAN.
Company Nodal Officer verifies documents within 30 days and submits Verification Report to IEPF Authority.
IEPF Authority sanction order issued; shares credited to Demat account and funds transferred to bank account via e-payment.

playbooks.expected_timeline: 60 to 90 calendar days post verification report submission

playbooks.title: 24-Hour Emergency Protocol for Unauthorized Trade Execution by Stock Broker
playbooks.legal_basis: SEBI Master Circular for Stock Brokers & Stock Exchange Investor Grievances Rules
playbooks.trigger_condition: Broker executes trade without explicit written/recorded client instruction or voice-recorded order confirmation

step_by_step_process.action: Immediately (within 24 hours) notify Stock Broker Compliance Officer and Designated Grievance Cell in writing (via registered email ID) stating unauthorized trade details.
Request immediate temporary freeze on trading terminal access and debit freeze on Demat account to prevent further unauthorized transactions.
If broker fails to reverse trade/losses within 48 hours, file a complaint on Stock Exchange Investor Grievance Portal (NSE: ignse@nse.co.in / BSE: investor.services@bseindia.com).
File complaint on SEBI SCORES 2.0 (scores.sebi.gov.in) attaching contract notes, voice recording logs, and email correspondence.
If unresolved, apply for Stock Exchange Investor Grievance Redressal Committee (IGRC) meeting or SMART ODR Arbitration.

playbooks.expected_timeline: 24 hours emergency report; 21 days for SCORES/Exchange resolution

playbooks.title: Compensation Claim for Delayed IPO ASBA Fund Unblocking
playbooks.jurisdiction: SEBI (SCSB Bank & Registrar to the Issue)
playbooks.trigger_condition: Self-Certified Syndicate Bank (SCSB) fails to unblock ASBA IPO application funds within T+1 day post-finalization of allotment

step_by_step_process.action: Check IPO allotment status on Registrar website (KFintech / Link Intime) to verify non-allotment.
Send written complaint to SCSB Bank Nodal Officer and Registrar specifying Application No, UPI ID/ASBA Account, and PAN.

Mandatory Compensation Clause: SCSB Bank is liable to pay compensation of Rs 100 per day of delay to the investor directly without requiring a formal request, for every day post-allotment finalization.
If bank/SCSB fails to unblock or pay compensation within 7 days, file complaint on SEBI SCORES 2.0 under IPO/ASBA category.

playbooks.title: Handling Non-Responsive Registrars and Transfer Agents (RTAs)
playbooks.legal_basis: SEBI Master Circular for Registrars to an Issue and Share Transfer Agents 2025
playbooks.trigger_condition: RTA (e.g. Link Intime, KFintech, Bigshare) fails to respond or process service request (demat, transmission, dividend, KYC) within 30 calendar days

step_by_step_process.action: Send formal reminder via registered email to RTA Compliance Officer citing initial SRN / inward reference number.
Lodge complaint on SEBI SCORES 2.0 (scores.sebi.gov.in) selecting the specific RTA and listed issuer company.
Under SCORES 2.0, the complaint is auto-routed to the RTA and its Designated Body (Depository/Exchange). RTA must submit Action Taken Report (ATR) within 21 calendar days.
If ATR is unsatisfactory, request First Level Review by Designated Body within 15 days, followed by SMART ODR if unresolved.

playbooks.title: Protocol for Trading App Crashes, Algorithmic Glitches, and Stop-Loss Failure
playbooks.jurisdiction: SEBI / Stock Exchange Standing Committee on Technology Glitches
playbooks.legal_basis: SEBI Framework for Handling Technical Glitches by Stock Brokers (Circular SEBI/HO/MIRSD/TPD-1/P/CIR/2022/160)
playbooks.trigger_condition: Broker trading platform crash, API outage, or order routing glitch preventing order execution or stop-loss execution during market hours

step_by_step_process.action: Take immediate timestamps, order logs, screenshot evidence, and call broker helpline to manually close positions if possible.
Submit formal complaint to Stock Broker within 24 hours attaching order IDs and system error logs.
Stock broker must log technical glitch event with Stock Exchange within 1 hour and submit Root Cause Analysis (RCA) report within 14 days.
If broker denies compensation for financial loss caused by system outage, escalate to Stock Exchange Investor Grievance Cell and SMART ODR.

playbooks.title: TDS Deduction on Dividends and Submission of Form 15G / 15H
playbooks.legal_basis: Section 194 of Income Tax Act 1961 read with CBDT Rules
playbooks.trigger_condition: Listed company deducts 10% or 20% TDS on dividend payouts exceeding Rs 5,000 in a financial year

step_by_step_process.action: Submit Form 15G (for individuals <60 yrs) or Form 15H (for senior citizens >=60 yrs) to Company RTA before record date to claim zero TDS deduction if total income is below taxable limit.
Ensure PAN is linked with Aadhaar; unlinked PAN attracts higher 20% TDS rate under Section 206AA.
If TDS has already been deducted and deposited with government, company/RTA cannot refund TDS directly. Investor must claim refund by filing Income Tax Return (ITR) for the financial year.

playbooks.title: Grievances Regarding Unlisted Shares, Pre-IPO Scams, and Unregistered Promoters
playbooks.jurisdiction: Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) / Civil Court / Cyber Crime
playbooks.trigger_condition: Promoter or unlisted dealer fails to deliver unlisted/pre-IPO shares or company vanishes after collecting funds

step_by_step_process.action: SEBI Jurisdiction Limitation: SEBI does not regulate unlisted private company transactions or off-market deals between individuals unless issued under public issue prospectus.
File complaint on MCA Portal (mca.gov.in) against Company Director/CIN under Companies Act Section 447 (Fraud).
If fake dealer / fake app involved in selling unlisted shares, file complaint on National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in / Helpline 1930).
